findings.F1: On days when the 20-day return is below 0, the next day's return minus the coin's mean falls steadily as the day's close moves up its high-low range. By close-location quintile it is +0.55 % (t 2.6), −0.06 %, −0.26 %, −0.54 % (t −2.7) and −0.80 % (t −4.2), about 735 cases each. The tested idea's close-location half is real and graded, and it runs both ways: a low close is followed by a rebound.
findings.F2: In the same falling-month days, the day's range multiple works against the idea. The widest-range quintile is followed by +0.35 % (t 1.35), the middle quintile by −0.65 % (t −3.6). The range weight adds size to the forecast exactly where the next-day fall vanishes.
findings.F3: In falling months, the next-day excess return also falls as the day's own 1-day return rises. By quintile it is +0.84 % (t 3.4), −0.11 %, −0.45 % (t −2.8), −0.78 % (t −4.1) and −0.61 % (t −3.0), about 735 cases each. That is a one-day reversal worth about 1.6 % from the lowest to the 4th quintile, against a 0.19 % cost per trade.
findings.F4: Over all days, on non-overlapping 5-day stretches, the 5-day excess return rises with how close the close sits to its 20-day high. By quintile of the distance to the high, from farthest to nearest, it is −0.37 %, −1.77 % (t −2.6), −1.33 % (t −2.3), +0.48 % and +3.50 % (t 4.7), about 285 cases each. The 20-day return gives the same picture: its 4th quintile shows +2.46 % (t 3.5) and its 2nd −2.58 % (t −4.2).
findings.F5: The book is a short bet on the market's own rise. On its worst-decile days the coins rose +6.3 %, and on its best-decile days they fell −7.2%. Its two worst windows, w10 and w11 (mean −0.07 % and −0.14 % a day), are the ones where the coins rose most (+0.40 % and +1.26 % a day).
findings.F6: The book's mean gain per active bar rises with the size of the short forecast, though weakly. The largest-forecast quintile earns +0.17 % (t 1.7) and the 4th earns −0.08 % (t −1.6). Most of the size the forecast carries adds little timing.

ideas.idea: While a coin's 20-day return is negative, the higher its 1-day close sits within that day's high-low range, the lower its return over the next 1 day, so a close near the day's low is followed by a rise and a close near the high by a fall.
ideas.consequence: Inside a falling month, a trader would lean short the day after a strong close and long the day after a weak close, in proportion to where the close sits in the day's range.
ideas.name: falling-month one-day close reversal

ideas.idea: While a coin's 20-day return is negative, the larger its 1-day return, the more it falls over the next 1 day, and the deeper its 1-day fall, the more it rebounds over the next 1 day.
ideas.consequence: In a falling month, a trader would fade each day's move into the next day, sizing by how large that move was.
ideas.name: falling-month daily return reversal

ideas.idea: The nearer a coin's daily close sits to its highest high of the past 20 days, the more the coin rises over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold a coin long for about a week in proportion to how close it closes to its 20-day high, and refuse shorts there.
ideas.name: near-high five-day continuation
